title: Cross-directory RenameFile dereferences a missing source
explanation: In VfsDirectoryServiceWrapper::RenameFile the null check on `src` exists only in the same-parent branch. When the guest renames a non-existent file into a different directory, `src` is nullptr and `src->GetSize()` is dereferenced, which crashes the emulator. The later ASSERT_MSG calls are soft (AssertFailSoftImpl does nothing unless Settings::values.use_debug_asserts is set), so a failed WriteBytes is also silently ignored and the source is then deleted, losing data.
suggested_fix: Move the `src == nullptr` check above the same-parent branch (return ResultPathNotFound). Check the WriteBytes result and return an error instead of relying on ASSERT_MSG; delete the source only after a verified copy.
how_to_verify: Call IFileSystem::RenameFile with a missing source path and a destination in another directory; the process faults at this line. Or read the function: there is no null check on the cross-directory path.

title: ExtractRomFS loops forever or recurses without bound on truncated or cyclic RomFS metadata
explanation: GetEntry returns a zero-initialised pair when the offset is outside the meta table, so sibling/child_dir/child_file read as 0, not ROMFS_ENTRY_EMPTY (0xFFFFFFFF). ProcessDirectory then reloads entry 0 forever (adding a VectorVfsDirectory to the parent each pass, so memory grows without bound) and the child_dir branch recurses until stack overflow. A cyclic sibling chain does the same, and ProcessFile has the same loop. There is no visited set or entry-count bound. ReadBytes of header.directory_meta.size and file_meta.size (u64 values taken from the file) also allocates before any bound check. Reachable from FSP_SRV::OpenDataFileSystemByCurrentProcess and OpenFileSystemWithPatch on a corrupt or hostile RomFS.
suggested_fix: Treat an out-of-range offset as an error (return failure from GetEntry and stop), bound the loops by the number of entries (meta size / minimum entry size), and reject meta sizes larger than the file.
how_to_verify: Build a RomFS whose directory_meta table has size 0 but a valid header and call ExtractRomFS; watch memory grow. Or unit-test GetEntry with an offset beyond the table size.

title: IFile::Read passes the guest size, not the buffer size, to the backend
explanation: The read length is the separate guest argument `size` (s64, cast to size_t, so a negative value becomes huge). Fsa::IFile::Read validates only null/offset/overflow and DoRead calls backend->Read(buffer, size, offset). The output buffer is a host ScratchBuffer sized to the guest buffer (cmif_serialization.h resize_destructive). A guest size larger than its buffer therefore writes past the host heap allocation. The scratch is also not zeroed and is copied back in full, so a short read at EOF returns stale host heap bytes to the guest. IStorage::Read (fs_i_storage.cpp) has the same pattern with `length`.
suggested_fix: Clamp size/length to out_buffer.size() and reject negative values with ResultInvalidSize; return an out-of-range result when offset+size passes the file size, or zero the unread tail.
how_to_verify: Issue IFile::Read with a size larger than the mapped buffer on a file smaller than size, in an ASan build. Reading cmif_serialization.h:348 and fs_i_file.cpp:29-39 shows no clamp.

title: KeyManager::LoadFromFile indexes fixed 0x20-entry keyblob arrays with a 2-hex-digit value
explanation: `keyblob_XX` and `encrypted_keyblob_XX` lines are parsed with strtoul of two hex digits (0..0xFF) and used to index std::array<..., 0x20> (key_manager.h:312-313). ValidCryptoRevisionString only checks that the characters are hex digits. A line such as `keyblob_ff = ...` in prod.keys writes out of bounds into KeyManager memory. HexStringToArray also has only a soft ASSERT_MSG for a too-short value and then reads str[i] past the end of the string, so a truncated key value gives garbage keys or an out-of-bounds read.
suggested_fix: Reject index >= keyblobs.size() before the store, and check out[1].size() >= 2*N before HexStringToArray.
how_to_verify: Put `keyblob_ff = ` followed by 144 hex digits into prod.keys and start the emulator under ASan or PageHeap; or compare the index range with the 0x20 array size.

title: NCZBLOCK header allocates up to 8 GiB from an unchecked block count
quote: const auto sizes = f->ReadBytes(static_cast<u64>(n) * 4, block_start + BlockFixed);
explanation: In ParseHeader the block count `n` (s32 from the file, only checked > 0) is multiplied by 4 and passed to VfsFile::ReadBytes, which does `std::vector<u8> out(size)` before reading. A corrupt or hostile .ncz with n near 2^31 requests about 8 GiB. The resulting std::bad_alloc or length_error is not caught in ParseHeader or OpenNcz (only the BlockReader constructor is wrapped), so it propagates out of RegisteredCache::InstallEntry and SubmissionPackage handling. Section offset and size are also taken as signed values from the file without a range check.
suggested_fix: Check `n * 4 <= fsize - block_start - BlockFixed` before the read and wrap OpenNcz in try/catch.
how_to_verify: Craft an NCZ with NCZBLOCK block count 0x7FFFFFFF and try to install or open it; expect an uncaught exception.

title: Fsa::IFile::DoWrite reports success when the write failed or the file is read-only
explanation: Fsa::IFile::Write never checks the open mode (DryWrite is unused), and DoWrite only does ASSERT_MSG(written == size). ASSERT_MSG is a soft assert: AssertFailSoftImpl does nothing unless Settings::values.use_debug_asserts is set. A write to a RomFS file or a read-opened RealVfsFile (returns 0) or on a full disk therefore returns ResultSuccess with no data written, and the guest believes its save was written. The real fs returns ResultWriteNotPermitted or a space error.
suggested_fix: Return ResultWriteNotPermitted when the file is not writable (use DryWrite with the open mode), and return a failure Result when written != size.
how_to_verify: Open a RomFS file through IFileSystem::OpenFile with Write mode and call IFile::Write; observe ResultSuccess and unchanged content.

title: NUP zstd members are fully decompressed on every cache miss with no in-flight de-duplication
explanation: Fork code. NupVfsFile::Read decompresses the whole member (up to cap/2 = 256 MiB) even for a read of a few bytes, outside the cache lock. Two threads missing the same member both read and decompress it and the second Insert is dropped, so work and memory are wasted. With a working set above the 512 MiB cap (streamed RomFS of a large title) the LRU thrashes and every read pays a full decompress. Members above cap/2 go to temp files; NupDecompressCache::spills is never evicted, so temp disk use grows with the number of large members touched, and `attempted` is set before the decompress, so one transient failure is permanent for that member.
suggested_fix: Add a per-member in-flight latch; decompress by zstd frame or block range where the codec allows, or lower the member size threshold; evict spill files; retry after a failed spill.
how_to_verify: Log timings in NupVfsFile::Read while a game streams two 200 MB zstd members alternately; or run a test with two threads reading the same uncached member.

title: IStorage read throttle sleeps on the shared fsp service thread
explanation: Fork code. IStorage::Read sleeps up to the charged cost of the previous read (64 KiB at 40 or 100 MB/s, roughly 1.6 or 0.65 ms) on the service thread that all fsp-srv sessions share, so save, SD and other IFile IPC wait behind it. On Windows sleep granularity (about 15.6 ms unless a finer timer period is active) can make the real delay far larger than intended, which lowers the effective rate below the configured value. The charge is also not carried as debt.
suggested_fix: Track the debt as a deadline and spin or yield for sub-millisecond waits, or throttle per session instead of blocking the shared thread.
how_to_verify: Measure achieved MB/s with EDEN_NX2_FS_READ_MBPS unset versus =0 on a game streaming 64 KiB reads.

title: Every read of a loose real file serialises on the global RealVfsFilesystem list_lock across disk I/O
explanation: RealVfsFile::Read holds the lock returned by RefreshReference (the filesystem-wide list_lock) through Seek and ReadSpan. All loose-RomFS or loose-file reads from any thread are therefore serialised and the lock is held during disk latency. A loose RomFS (OffsetVfsFile over one RealVfsFile per file) streaming from several threads gets no I/O concurrency.
suggested_fix: Hold list_lock only to look up and refresh the FILE*, pin it with a per-reference refcount, and do the read under a per-file lock.
how_to_verify: Stream a loose RomFS from two threads and compare throughput with one thread.

title: Solid NCZ install keeps the whole decompressed NCA in memory
explanation: SolidNczFile appends every decoded chunk to `data` and never frees earlier bytes, even though install reads are sequential. Installing a multi-GB solid .ncz (RegisteredCache::RawInstallNCA with DecompressNCZForInstall) needs the full NCA size in RAM on a 16 GB machine, and vector reallocation transiently needs about 2x.
suggested_fix: Keep a sliding window (drop data before the last requested offset) or decode to a temporary file.
how_to_verify: Install a 4+ GB solid NCZ and watch the working set.

title: RegisteredCache::RawInstallNCA overwrite path dereferences a null file for non-canonical layouts
explanation: GetFileAtID probes several layouts (flat /{id}.nca, 00/01 split directory, two-digit directories) but the overwrite branch only resolves the canonical GetRelativePathFromNcaID path. If the existing NCA was found in another layout, GetFileRelative(path) returns nullptr and the call crashes. The canonical-layout case works.
suggested_fix: Delete the file that GetFileAtID returned, and null-check before use.
how_to_verify: Place an NCA in a flat /{ncaid}.nca layout in the registered directory and install the same id with overwrite_if_exists.

title: RegisteredCache::Refresh never clears meta, meta_id or yuzu_meta
explanation: ProcessFiles only inserts. After RemoveExistingEntry or Delete followed by Refresh, GetEntryVersion and IterateAllMetadata still see the removed title (metadata is emitted without checking that the NCA still exists). InstallEntry also removes the old entry before the new install can fail with ErrorCopyFailed, which loses the old content. Upstream yuzu behaves the same.
suggested_fix: Clear the three maps at the start of Refresh, and install to a temporary name before removing the old entry.
how_to_verify: Install, delete and Refresh a title, then call GetEntryVersion for it.
